content.user_title: Design Rust Port and Adapter Boundaries
content.value_statement: External services can leak infrastructure concerns into domain code. This skill helps design Rust traits and adapters that keep dependencies isolated and testable.
actual_capabilities: Designs Rust trait ports for repositories, payment gateways, and notification services.
Shows adapter patterns for PostgreSQL, HTTP clients, and in-memory tests.
Uses async_trait, Send, and Sync patterns for async Rust services.
Maps infrastructure errors into domain-specific error types.
Suggests boundaries for databases, APIs, file systems, and other external systems.
Describes testing strategies with in-memory or mock adapters.
limitations: Provides patterns and examples, not a complete framework or generated project.
Example types such as UserId, Money, and RepositoryError must be defined by the user.
Repository-specific advice requires the assistant to read the relevant project files.
Does not validate runtime credentials, network behavior, or database schemas.

use_cases.title: Decouple Persistence
use_cases.description: Move direct SQLx usage behind repository traits and keep domain logic independent from the database.

use_cases.title: Plan Hexagonal Architecture
use_cases.description: Define ports and adapters before adding external APIs, queues, file stores, or payment services.

use_cases.title: Improve Testability
use_cases.description: Create in-memory adapters or mocks so application services can be tested without production infrastructure.

prompt_templates.title: Identify a Port
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one dependency boundary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the external dependency in this Rust module and suggest the smallest useful port trait for it.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Rust adapter for this port. Include construction, error mapping, async behavior, and ownership choices.

prompt_templates.title: Add Test Doubles
prompt_templates.scenario: Make domain services easier to test.
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest in-memory or mock adapters for these ports and explain which behaviors each test should cover.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Boundary
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration from coupled infrastructure code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Rust service and propose a step-by-step refactor to ports and adapters without changing behavior.

output_examples.input: A Rust service calls SQLx queries directly from domain logic.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies a repository port, a PostgreSQL adapter, an in-memory test adapter, and domain error mapping.

output_examples.input: A payment workflow needs Stripe integration without coupling the domain layer to reqwest.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a payment gateway port, a Stripe adapter outline, error categories, and test double guidance.

output_examples.input: A notification feature must support email now and SMS later.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a focused notification port with separate adapters for each provider and shared domain results.

best_practices: Keep port traits focused on domain actions, not vendor APIs.
Use domain types and domain errors at every boundary.
Add test adapters before wiring production infrastructure.
anti_patterns: Expose database rows or HTTP response types through domain traits.
Create large gateway traits that combine unrelated external systems.
Let adapters return raw infrastructure errors to application services.

faq.question: What architecture style does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports hexagonal architecture and ports-and-adapters patterns for Rust applications.

faq.question: Can it design database repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes repository port guidance and PostgreSQL adapter patterns.

faq.question: Can it help with external APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline HTTP client adapters and service ports for external systems.

faq.question: Does it generate complete working applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides design patterns and implementation guidance that must be adapted to a project.

faq.question: Is it useful for tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends in-memory adapters and mocks for isolated service tests.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
